source: docs/METROPOLIS-MASTER-v2.1.md (Master Design Document v2.1 incl. Amendment A1)
authoring: Hand-authored single source of truth. tools/plan/generate.js derives code.json and tools/plan/bow-import.json from this file — never edit those outputs directly (GR#3). Sequence numbers are gapped by ~10 to allow insertions. v1.1.0 (2026-08-08): sprint assignments S0-S11 added (cloud/future items unscheduled); tool.bow decision enacted; tool.planguard + tool.ready added; engine.comms resequenced after engine.firms.

naming.moduleKey: dot-separated lowercase: <layer>.<name> (e.g. engine.traffic, ui.widgets); matches BOW mkey and code.json key
naming.goPackages: internal/engine/<name>, internal/ui/<name>, internal/protocol, internal/foundation/<name>; cmd/metropolis, cmd/bow, cmd/metctl
naming.specRef: References §, UI-SPEC §, M0-ENG §, A-amendments and Part IV sections of docs/METROPOLIS-MASTER-v2.1.md

universalEdges.note: These call edges apply to every module and are NOT repeated per item to keep the graph readable; they are as binding as explicit edges.
edges: * -> foundation.errors : every module raises registry-sourced errors with correlation IDs and writes structured NDJSON logs (GR#1, GR#7)
engine.* -> foundation.det : all randomness via counter-based hash streams; all parallelism via the 256-shard phase-barrier scheme (§1.2)
engine.* -> foundation.registry : every engine module registers with a mandatory Stub implementation (M0-ENG §2)
ui.screen.* -> int.protocol : screens consume engine state ONLY via view subscriptions; their calls list names the engine modules whose projections they subscribe to, transport is always the protocol

errorHandling.registry: data/errors.json — every error code declared before use; format MET-<layer><NNN> (F=foundation, P=protocol, E=engine, U=ui, T=tooling), e.g. MET-E042. No ad-hoc error construction anywhere (GR#7).
errorHandling.correlation: Every protocol command carries a correlationId (UUID, minted by the initiating side). It propagates through engine events, deltas, logs and error records so any failure is traceable end-to-end (GR#1).
errorHandling.logging: Structured NDJSON: logs/engine.ndjson + logs/ui.ndjson, rotated. Error entries: {ts, level, code, correlationId, module, msg, ctx}. F12 info panel tails them live; metctl errors gives offline review. Errors are stored, never printed-and-lost.
errorHandling.display: Selectable error display per GR#1: every user-visible failure shows its registry code + correlation ID.

conventions.determinism: Same seed + same command log => bit-identical world at any worker count (§1.2). 256 fixed shards, ordered merges, Philox-style counter RNG keyed (worldSeed, entityId, month, purpose), int64 micro-pounds, no map-range on tick paths (lint-enforced, A8). CI determinism gate is written FIRST (M0-ENG §6.4).

items.title: Planning pipeline: master plan -> code.json generator -> BOW import
items.desc: docs/planning/master-plan-v2.1.json as SSOT; tools/plan/generate.js mints stable GUIDs (module + inbound + outbound), computes forward/reverse call pointers, emits code.json and the BOW import file; claude-bow.js import loads the metro BOW idempotently.

items.title: Engine<->UI protocol v1: commands, events, deltas, view subscriptions
items.desc: Versioned message schema (BuyLand, SetBudget, AdvanceTicks...; state deltas + events out), correlation IDs on every command, view-subscription contract (named projections, deltas only for live subscriptions — also the remote-play seam). In-process channels v1, gRPC transport implemented but dormant behind a config flag.

inbound.name: ProtocolV1
inbound.pattern: versioned command/event/delta envelope with correlationId

items.title: StateSerializer + save/fixture schema (NDJSON shards, binary at scale, metctl export)
items.desc: StateSerializer interface from day one (A3): sharded gzipped NDJSON canonical for configs/fixtures/exports and small saves; versioned binary shard snapshots above a size threshold; metctl export produces lossless NDJSON from any binary save. Save format IS the fixture format. Header carries version + debug-touched flag + migration rules.

inbound.name: StateSerializer
inbound.pattern: pluggable NDJSON/binary backends, version-tagged shards

items.title: Solver contract: CPU/GPU/cloud interchangeable offload seam
items.desc: Stateless request/response contract for traffic equilibrium, cold-pass batches, deep projections and batch life-writing, with local fallback. Zone-aggregated OD sizing tables live here (A4). The engine cannot tell CPU from GPU from cloud except by latency (A9).

inbound.name: SolverContract
inbound.pattern: stateless request/response, backend-agnostic, local fallback mandatory

items.title: Error registry, correlation IDs, structured logging, stored error review
items.desc: Registry-sourced errors only (data/errors.json, codes MET-<layer><NNN>); correlation ID propagation end-to-end; structured NDJSON logs (logs/engine.ndjson, logs/ui.ndjson, rotated); errors persisted for review via F12 tail and metctl errors. The foundation every other module's error handling is built on (GR#1, GR#7).

inbound.name: ErrsAPI
inbound.pattern: errs.New(code, correlationId, ctx) — the only legal error constructor

items.title: Go monorepo skeleton + CI pipeline + build-info injection
items.desc: Monorepo layout (cmd/, internal/, data/, fixtures/, tools/, docs/, sql/); trunk-based git with conventional commits carrying BoW refs; CI: build, go vet, golangci-lint (custom determinism rules), escape-analysis gate, gctrace perf gate, UI snapshot tests, invariant suite, perf smoke; version/commit/branch/timestamp injected via -ldflags, never hand-maintained.

items.title: Determinism core: 256 shards, phase barriers, counter RNG, fixed-point money
items.desc: 256 fixed shards (spatial for cells/network, id-hash for citizens/firms), shard-order 0->255 merges, phase barriers with (shard, sequence)-ordered cross-shard messages, Philox-style counter RNG keyed (worldSeed, entityId, month, purpose), int64 micro-pounds, fixed-order float summation where unavoidable.

inbound.name: DetAPI
inbound.pattern: hash-stream draws + shard scheduler; no shared RNG object anywhere

items.title: Module registry: real/stub/off status, health, CanToggle — one registry, two consumers
items.desc: Every simulation module registers behind an interface with a mandatory Stub implementation; engine boots with any real/stub mix; registry rows carry name, semver, status, health, last-tick cost, feature-flag source; F12 info panel is a view of the same registry with guarded toggles.

inbound.name: RegistryAPI
inbound.pattern: Register(module, stub); status transitions emit world-events

items.title: Config data files + loader + debug hot-reload
items.desc: data/consumption.json, modes.json, buildings.json, unlock_trees.json, naming_corpus.json, seasonal.json, external_world.json, policies.json, errors.json — all JSON, hot-reloadable in debug, the entire balance surface for M2 Batch tuning. Validators derive expected values from these files, never hardcoded (GR#15).

inbound.name: DataAPI
inbound.format: Go package API over JSON files
inbound.pattern: typed loaders + schema validation + hot-reload hook

items.title: BOW git integration on the metro BOW (decision: no separate metropolis_bow DB)
items.desc: DECIDED (Aaron, 2026-08-08): the metro BOW (claude-bow.js) IS the project Book of Work — it now carries the spec's fields (seq/sprint/milestone/spec_ref/GUIDs/deps) so building the separate metropolis_bow schema of M0-ENG §4 would duplicate SSOT (GR#3). Remaining work from that section: commit-msg validation that [mkey] refs exist in the BOW, auto-comment of commit hashes onto items (extend claude-pre-commit-check.js or a commit hook), and the F12 read-only BoW tab (already in ui.screen.debug).

items.title: H-STUB StubEngine + Folkestone-64 fixture + chaos knobs
items.desc: Full protocol implementation with canned behaviour: static handcrafted 64x64 world, accepts commands, scripted/recorded delta streams, obeys speed controls with fake ticks; chaos knobs (delayed/burst deltas) prove UI budgets under stress. The UI is built against H-STUB from week one. Permanent fixture.

inbound.name: StubEngine
inbound.pattern: canned world + scripted deltas + chaos injection

items.title: TUI renderer core: cell-buffer diff, decoupled loops, capability probe
items.desc: tcell; front/back styled cell buffers with diff flushing (no clears, flicker structurally impossible); T-INPUT (<10ms echo) / T-RENDER (10Hz + on-input) / T-VIEWS (delta subscription client, double-buffered view models); Windows Terminal primary, conhost degraded profile by capability probe; min 120x30, reflow on resize; zero-allocation draw paths on hot widgets. UI holds views, never the world (<150MB).

inbound.name: UICoreAPI
inbound.pattern: single-goroutine screen ownership (T-RENDER); widgets draw to back buffer only

items.title: Widget library: sparklines, Braille charts, heatmaps, gauges, tables, queue lanes
items.desc: The shared visual grammar: box-drawing borders, semantic + colourblind palettes (day one), 12-cell sparklines, Braille 2x4 sub-grid charts (projections with confidence bands, month-age pyramid), background-ramp heatmaps, block gauges, big-num tiles with delta arrows, sortable/filterable/CSV-exportable tables, literal truck-queue lanes per junction approach, 300ms threshold pulse.

inbound.name: WidgetAPI
inbound.format: Go package API on shared cell-buffer
inbound.pattern: custom widgets over UICoreAPI; no allocation on draw paths

items.title: Key grammar: leader sequences, which-key HUD, palette, marks, remappable keymaps
items.desc: Verb->noun->variant leader language (b r s, z d h...), which-key HUD within one UI tick that dims as sequences are learned, vim counts/repeat (5 b r s, .), undo/redo where engine permits, 12 map marks, / name search over auto-named objects, fuzzy command palette with key sequences printed beside actions + parameterised commands (:loan 5M 10y), globals (Space, 1/2/3, o, ?, !), optional mouse with a key path for everything. Keymaps stored as JSON profile data.

inbound.name: KeyGrammar
inbound.format: Go package API + keymap JSON schema
inbound.pattern: leader-key state machine; every action registered with mnemonic path

items.title: Engine orchestrator: two-layer clock, deterministic phase pipeline, shard worker pool
items.desc: One day-night cycle per calendar month; 30 daily logistics ticks per cycle; monthly tick in fixed phases (production -> logistics settlement -> consumption & shortfall -> population -> land value & decay -> finance); speeds pause/1x/2x/4x (8x debug), secondsPerMonthAt1x=480 master pacing knob; POOL-SIM (NumCPU-2) stealing fixed shards; pre-sized arenas, zero heap allocation steady-state; T-SUBSCR view-subscription server; T-PERSIST copy-on-write snapshots off the tick path; no wall-clock time in logic, ever.

inbound.name: EngineAPI
inbound.pattern: command in -> phase pipeline -> deltas/events out; phases are barriers

items.title: Determinism CI gate — the first test written
items.desc: Same seed, 120 months, twice: sha256(worldSnapshot) must match; again with POOL-SIM=1 vs =14; mismatch fails the build. Built and passing on the stub engine BEFORE any simulation logic (TDD order explicit per A8). Determinism bugs are always P0.

items.title: F1 Map screen: viewport, minimap, overlays, inspect, follow
items.desc: Scrollable viewport + minimap; overlay cycle (ownership, land value, zoning, utilities, traffic, pollution, decay, per-service coverage, parking occupancy, vitality); Enter inspects any cell/building/citizen, f follows a citizen; foreground glyph = structure/terrain, background = metric (two data layers per cell).

items.title: Walking skeleton: playable-looking nothing, end-to-end
items.desc: Protocol + registry + stub-everything engine + H-STUB + determinism gate + F1 map on fixture, running the full pipeline end-to-end before any real model. Then modules go real one at a time in BOW seq order.

items.title: F12 info panel: build/runtime stats, module registry view + toggles, error tail, phase timing, BoW tab
items.desc: Build & code info (ldflags-injected), runtime (uptime, memory vs budget table, GC pauses, goroutines, channel depths, input-echo p99), module registry rows with guarded ON/OFF/STUB toggles, last-50 error tail pretty-printing the NDJSON logs, per-phase µs sparkline over 60 ticks, read-only BoW tab (open counts by priority).

items.title: Debug as a runtime feature switch
items.desc: Release builds carry it, default off; enable via --debug, config, or :debug on; switching ON is recorded in the save header forever (balance data hygiene); unlocks 8x speed, cheats (free money, instant build, force milestone), entity JSON inspector, fidelity-dial exposure, console, fixture record/replay controls.

items.title: H-REPLAY: recorded command/delta fixtures
items.desc: Delta streams and command logs recorded from any engine (stub or real) into fixtures/*.ndjson.gz; replayable into the UI (stable data for UX work) and into the engine (regression: replay commands, compare snapshots). Permanent fixture.

items.title: Headless UI test harness: scripted keys, snapshot asserts, latency budgets
items.desc: Drives the widget layer with scripted key sequences against recorded delta streams and asserts cell-buffer snapshots; UI-SPEC §5 latency budgets asserted in CI (keystroke echo <10ms, screen switch <30ms, diff flush <3ms typical).

items.title: H-HEADLESS: engine without UI
items.desc: metropolis -headless -seed N -months M -out snap.json + scenario scripts (JSON command lists); emits per-phase timing and invariant reports every tick. The balance/Batch/CI workhorse.

items.title: H-SYNTH: synthetic world generator + perf CI
items.desc: Parametric cities (population, sprawl, network shape) for perf/scale testing; know the 10M-citizen tick cost in month 3 of development; perf CI graphs tick-time vs scale per commit; a commit regressing monthly-tick time >10% at the 1M-citizen synthetic fails.

items.title: Tile georeference: OS grid squares for start tile and expansion extent
items.desc: Exact OS Terrain 50 grid squares for the 2x2km Folkestone West–Seabrook start tile and the ~60x60km East Kent expansion extent (Dover–Ashford–Dungeness). Open item V.2.5.

items.title: World & terrain: OS Terrain 50 import, cells, slope, geology, hydrology, tile expansion
items.desc: Build-time heightmap from OS Terrain 50 downsampled to 10m cells (~30B core: elevation, slope class, surface, ownership, zoning, structure ref, land value, overlay scratch); slope class multiplies build cost and gates types; geology layer (chalk, clay pockets, gravels, deep coal east) gates mining; terrain flow model derives Pent/Seabrook hydrology; 2x2km purchasable tiles, only owned tiles fully simulated; motorway + one junction survive the wipe.

inbound.name: WorldAPI
inbound.pattern: cell/tile queries, ownership mutations via commands only

items.title: Citizens Option B: persistent individuals, adaptive fidelity, no culls ever
items.desc: ~250B hot record (month birthdate, household, home/work/school, 8-axis personality, education-drifted, derived leisure tastes, health bands, wealth, employment, satisfaction); cold store columnar SoA, field-compressed 60-100B (A1); HOT/WARM/COLD dial with amortised 1/30-shards-per-day cold pass (A2); cold parameters ONLY from the stratified rotating sample, camera-invariance a CI invariant (A7); binding deterministic life-writing on inspection; per-person Gompertz-Makeham monthly mortality hazards; NVMe stated requirement >20M local.

inbound.name: CitizensAPI
inbound.pattern: hot AoS / cold SoA; every stochastic draw hash(worldSeed, id, month, purpose)

items.title: Invariant checker: conservation asserts every tick
items.desc: People, money, goods and vehicles must balance — hard assert in dev builds, logged registry error in release; vehicle-conservation makes despawn-masking structurally impossible (§19.3); runs in H-HEADLESS reports and CI invariant suite.

inbound.name: InvariantAPI
inbound.format: Go package API: RegisterStock(name string, snapshot func() int64) called once per conserved stock at module init
inbound.pattern: each registered stock's per-tick delta must equal tracked ins minus outs (conservation of people/money/goods/vehicles, §14, §19.3); violation is a hard assert in dev builds, a registry error in release

items.title: Needs & commodities behind the Market interface
items.desc: Water, power, gas, food staple/fresh, fuel, materials, goods, waste — each importable (opex, logistics capacity in tonnes/slots), locally producible (capex + land + jobs + inputs) or hybrid; static import prices v1 behind a Market interface so dynamic pricing is a config flip; services (non-tradable) declared separately.

inbound.name: MarketAPI
inbound.pattern: price/availability queries; dynamic-world future hook

items.title: Consumption coefficients + four utility networks
items.desc: Coefficient-driven demand (class coefficients x occupancy/throughput from data/consumption.json — catalogue never hard-codes utility numbers); water, wastewater (95% rule), electricity, gas as separate networks with sources, pipes/wires (free in road corridors), storage and losses; aquifer sustainable-yield ceiling and degradation; peak vs base load; all-electric strategy viable.

inbound.name: UtilityAPI
inbound.pattern: network solve per daily tick; coefficients from DataAPI

items.title: Economy & finance: money flows, land market, loans, credit rating, insolvency
items.desc: Household income -> taxes -> budget -> opex/imports/debt/construction; simple firm P&L opening/closing on profitability (v1, superseded by engine.firms); continuous land pricing base x access x amenity x scarcity; loan facilities by milestone, interest from credit rating f(debt/revenue, history, reserves); refinancing spiral; insolvency (3 months unable to meet obligations, no credit) = game over; investment programmes with multi-year payback in projections. Int64 micro-pounds everywhere.

inbound.name: FinanceAPI
inbound.pattern: double-entry ledger; every figure drill-through to ledger lines

items.title: Routing & traffic: SUE assignment, junction models, spillback, mode logit, commute accounting
items.desc: Daily capacity-restrained stochastic user equilibrium on the road graph with zone-aggregated OD (~10^3-10^4 zones, A4) — never citizen-pair routing; volume-delay functions, cached warm starts, contraction hierarchies; lanes are link capacity (no lane-choice pathology); junction control types (priority/mini-rbt/roundabout/signals with splits), turn-movement capacities, queue spillback blocking upstream; nothing despawns; per-trip nested logit over 13 modes, personality-weighted, real hills for bikes; door-to-door commute times stored per citizen (hot)/district (cold); freight shares the network as PCUs; induced demand emerges from latent-demand pool.

inbound.name: TrafficAPI
inbound.pattern: assignment via int.solver (CPU v1); results deterministic, cache contents-independent

items.title: Roads & auto-naming: named edges, class ladder, maintenance, upgrades, roadworks
items.desc: Roads as named edges with identity (class ladder alley->motorway, lanes, speed limits, maintenance state — potholes cost); deterministic auto-naming for EVERY object from seed+id (Kentish corpus x suffix, continuation rules; civic buildings named for notable deceased citizens; functional numbering; transit auto-lettering), player-renameable; in-place upgrades with simulated roadworks (phased lane closures re-routing real traffic, warned in projections); road inspector shows volume, v/c, top-5 OD flows and alternatives.

inbound.name: RoadsAPI
inbound.pattern: graph mutations via commands; naming registry service for all modules

items.title: Logistics & JIT: stocks, replenishment, junction slots, trucks, lead times
items.desc: Daily tick: consumers draw from local stock (capacity, holding cost, shelf life); stock managers order against forecast + player-tunable safety buffer (lean/fat per commodity); orders become truck movements on the road graph; finite junction slots/day with literal queue render; import lead times (road days, sea 10x bulk); perishables expire in queue; shortfalls hit satisfaction, health, production, construction. The beating heart.

inbound.name: LogisticsAPI
inbound.pattern: order book + movement scheduler; queue states subscribable per junction

items.title: Zoning (8-way) & construction: land purchase, build queue, materials, lead times, demolition
items.desc: Zone types Dwelling/Shop/Office/Entertainment/Farming/Manufacturing/Heavy Industry/Mining with demand bars that explain themselves (no labour, no power, no freight); construction consumes materials + labour + junction capacity with seasonal speed; lead times; demolition + compensation; land purchase before building.

inbound.name: BuildAPI
inbound.pattern: build orders are commands; queue visible; catalogue-driven from buildings.json

items.title: Seasonality: month-index curves for every seasonal system
items.desc: Winter power peak, summer water stress, harvest calendar lumps, winter construction slowdown, September school intake gate, seaside leisure/tourism curve, winter health wave — all curves in data/seasonal.json and visible in projections.

inbound.name: SeasonAPI
inbound.pattern: pure functions of month index from seasonal.json

items.title: Households & housing typologies: formation, appeal profiles, mismatch
items.desc: Real households (partnering among hot/sampled, calibrated statistical among cold); demand = households x dwelling-size preference; 17 housing typologies with appeal profiles over household stage x wealth x personality — citywide demand is a distribution over types, a city of identical blocks leaves personality segments unhoused-by-preference; overcrowding and rent burden feed satisfaction and migration.

inbound.name: HouseholdsAPI
inbound.pattern: typology appeal from buildings.json profiles

items.title: Attractiveness & migration — the master dial
items.desc: A = w1*jobAvailability(skill-matched) + w2*housingAffordability + w3*serviceCoverage + w4*environment + w5*leisureFit(venue mix vs migrant personality distribution) + w6*safety + w7*reputation(momentum); monthly net migration g(A - A_world) x capacity constraints (housing vacancy, junction arrival throughput); per-resident personality-weighted emigration; reputation momentum is the Detroit trap asymmetry. World pool infinite/static v1 behind the future hook.

inbound.name: AttractAPI
inbound.pattern: term-decomposed A score, every term drill-through

items.title: Failure states: Detroit spiral, abandonment, blight spread, ghost-city ending
items.desc: Shock -> emigration -> tax base down -> cuts/debt -> attractiveness down -> more emigration -> abandoned buildings (decay state: neighbour land-value drag, hazard/fire/crime pressure, demolition cost) -> district blight spreading cell-by-cell; recovery expensive but possible; death: insolvency, or population <10% of historic peak after ever exceeding 50k — epilogue from the history log. No scripted loss.

inbound.name: DecayAPI
inbound.pattern: decay states on cells/buildings; spiral metrics subscribable

items.title: Projections engine + the Slow-Fuse Principle
items.desc: Every demand/supply curve N years forward (N grows with unlocked forecasting; cloud offload extends), seasonally aware, with queued-decision markers (a planned school appears as a capacity step BEFORE it's built); Slow-Fuse (A5): any decision whose principal effects land >5 game-years out MUST render its projected consequence in the confirmation UI at decision time — binding across all systems. The anti-ambush machine.

inbound.name: ProjectionsAPI
inbound.pattern: systems register curve providers; UI subscribes to named projections

items.title: Unlock economy: XP, 13-milestone ladder, development-point trees, direct buy
items.desc: XP earned continuously; milestones Wilderness(0)->Centopolis(100M win) each granting unlocks, cash, expansion permits, loan uplift, Development Points; per-category progression trees (12 'Blue'-style categories) from unlock_trees.json; off-map capacity always purchasable with money (grid/gas/rail/port/water tranches); cheat/debug force-unlock for testing.

inbound.name: UnlocksAPI
inbound.pattern: gate checks data-driven from unlock_trees.json (GR#15)

items.title: Service framework: capacity + coverage + funding-quality, staffing pools, Public Service Pie
items.desc: Generic service model (education, healthcare, elder care, fire, police, deathcare, leisure, transport...): capacity, coverage radius, funding level -> quality; shared staffing pools (a nurse shortage is one shortage everywhere); Public Service Pie per-1k benchmark ratios (police ~2.4, teachers, nurses, refuse crews, council officers) with consequences scaling from village-mild to city-systemic; upgrade paths per catalogue.

inbound.name: ServicesAPI
inbound.pattern: per-service capacity/demand/coverage; funding sliders are commands

items.title: Wellbeing: physical & mental health tracks with causal drivers
items.desc: Two 0-100 per-citizen tracks. Physical: age curve, healthcare access/quality/waiting lists, diet (fresh-food share), active travel, pollution exposure, sport x physicality. Mental: commute time (nonlinear past 45min — the biggest modifiable hit), job-ambition mismatch, green space within 400m, leisure-fit, crowding, isolation (sociability x community access), noise, financial stress (rent >35%), unemployment duration. Drives mortality, productivity, satisfaction, emigration. Wellbeing = f(physical, mental, satisfaction) is the headline stat.

inbound.name: WellbeingAPI
inbound.pattern: driver-decomposed scores; every driver drill-through

items.title: External commuting: finite off-map job pools, dormitory arithmetic
items.desc: Off-map jobs (London/Ashford/Dover) with FINITE era-scaled capacity (A6) reachable via motorway or external rail (fast, expensive, big capacity); city collects income tax without providing the job — dormitory strategy viable early, capped by pool size, rail/coach crowding, commute mental-health burden, and structurally thin revenue (no rates/corp share — surfaced in F2 incidence); in-commuting fills labour shortage with visible wage leakage.

inbound.name: ExtCommuteAPI
inbound.pattern: pools from external_world.json; era scaling

items.title: buildings.json: the full Part IV catalogue encoded
items.desc: Every object from catalogue sections R/E/W/H/ED/F-P/G/PK/L/T/PT/HS/C-I/LM/CM-WF plus supplements 1-3 (security & justice, farming & food, mining, comms & logistics, business & finance, FDI anchors, fuel & chemicals, rail industry, destination, tunnelling, health splits, civic, defence, mega-projects) with unlock gates, costs, capacities, coefficients refs, blight class, appeal profiles. Coefficients live in consumption.json — the catalogue never hard-codes utility numbers (§17).

items.title: Save/load UX: manual, rolling yearly autosave, milestone saves
items.desc: Manual save anytime, autosave every game year (rolling 10), milestone saves; save header carries version + debug-touched flag; F10 menu integration; large saves stream via StateSerializer without loading whole worlds.

items.title: Disasters-lite: event pressure on JIT
items.desc: Road closure, storm surge on shore cells, aquifer drought — never random-spam, projected where possible, resolved through the same logistics/dispatch machinery.

items.title: Balance harness: parameter sweeps, pacing tuning to achievable-but-hard
items.desc: Thousands of parameter runs, centuries per run, over data/*.json (the whole balance surface): local sweep runner first, Azure Batch when needed; tunes secondsPerMonthAt1x, growth curves, milestone spacing until 0->100M is achievable-but-hard in 80-150 hours.

inbound.name: SweepRunner
inbound.pattern: H-HEADLESS fan-out; results comparable across seeds

items.title: Diagram engines: chain diagrams, network schematics, text Sankey
items.desc: Three auto-laid-out block-text engines: production chains as boxes/arrows with live t/day on arrows; power/water/chemical grids as node-edge schematics with load colouring + tube-map transit strips; text Sankey for the Fiscal Circuit (proportional block-width money bands). Layered graph drawing, small n, cached until topology changes.

inbound.name: DiagramAPI
inbound.pattern: topology in, cell-buffer layout out; cache keyed on topology hash

items.title: Dashboards, layout editor, drill-through rule
items.desc: Widget grid (bignum, gauge, sparkline chart, table, mini-map, alert list) with shipped layouts per screen and a user layout editor saved in profile JSON; THE DRILL-THROUGH RULE (absolute): every number on every screen is selectable and Enter goes to its source — no dead ends, the whole UI one navigable graph.

inbound.name: DashAPI
inbound.format: Go package API + layout JSON schema
inbound.pattern: tiles bind to view-model paths; drill targets registered per binding

items.title: Top bar + prioritised alert stack + crisis auto-pause
items.desc: Persistent chrome: date, clock-cycle, speed, money, population, rating; bottom alert stack — prioritised, colour-coded, each alert jumps to its screen; ! jumps to top alert; crisis events auto-pause and drop camera/speed to the relevant queue.

items.title: F2 Finance: P&L, balance sheet, loans, rating, budget sliders + fiscal-circuit master view
items.desc: Full finance screen plus the §54 top-down Sankey (money enters via exports/tourism/out-commuter wages/FDI/grants, leaves via imports/leakage/interest), tax instrument panel with elasticity curves and incidence display (who actually pays), gross-vs-net public payroll truth.

items.title: F3 Land & Construction screen
items.desc: Purchase, zone, build queue (materials + labour + lead time), demolition; catalogue browser driven by buildings.json with unlock state.

items.title: F4 Services screen
items.desc: Per-service funding slider, capacity vs demand, coverage map jump, response-time distributions, waiting lists, Public Service Pie allocation.

items.title: F5 Trade & Logistics screen
items.desc: Import contracts, junction queue live view (the signature truck-glyph image), warehouse stock/buffer policy per commodity, port when unlocked, balance-of-trade extension (t/day and £/day by commodity and artery), pipeline-vs-truck safety trade view.

items.title: F6 Demographics screen
items.desc: Month-age ASCII population pyramid (smooth), education pipeline, workforce by sector/skill vs demand (white/blue collar), personality & leisure-taste distributions, 'how your city spends Saturday' hours-by-activity view, housing demand-vs-stock by typology, in/out-commuting leak view.

items.title: F7 Projections screen
items.desc: Every demand/supply curve N years forward: history solid Braille, projection dim, confidence bands, threshold lines, queued-decision markers; contracted-vs-internal demand crossings (§36); rate outlook (§45); Slow-Fuse confirmations render here.

items.title: F9 Ticker & History screen

items.title: Plan-drift guard hook: commits blocked when code.json is stale
items.desc: claude-plan-guard.js (PreToolUse on git commit): runs tools/plan/generate.js --check, then regenerates to a temp path and diffs against the committed code.json/bow-import.json — a hand-edit of generated files or a master-plan change without regeneration blocks the commit with the exact drift shown. Defect class eliminated: plan/registry divergence (GR#3, GR#6).

items.title: Secret & hardcoding guard hook: commits blocked when staged content carries credentials or GR#15 violations
items.desc: claude-secret-guard.js (PreToolUse on git commit): scans STAGED content (git diff --cached) for secrets — private key blocks, API key/token patterns, passwords in URLs/connection strings, high-entropy literals — and hardcoding smells (GR#15: expected counts/values as literals in validator-shaped code). Fail-closed on detection with per-line evidence; CLAUDE_DISABLE_SECRET_GUARD=1 escape hatch (same posture as tool.planguard); allowlist file for sanctioned patterns (e.g. the documented localhost/root/no-password metro DB default, UUID literals). Mechanises GR#11's secrets half so it no longer depends on lead vigilance.

items.title: BOW ready-to-build view: claude-bow.js ready + /sprint skill
items.desc: The v_ready_to_build equivalent for the metro BOW: `node claude-bow.js ready` lists open items with no open dependencies grouped by sprint in seq order; .claude/commands/sprint.md skill surfaces it with the working-agreement rule 'always work from ready, never start a blocked item' (M0-ENG §6.2).

items.title: Codename discipline guard hook: commits/pushes blocked when the reference title's real name reaches git
items.desc: claude-codename-guard.js (PreToolUse on git commit/push): enforces GR#22 — the reference title is 'Blue' and only 'Blue'; its real name, abbreviations and numbered form must never enter git (code, data, docs, comments, commit messages, branch names). Scans staged added lines (git diff --cached), the commit message/command text, and the current branch name; patterns are assembled from fragments at runtime so the guard's own source never carries the forbidden literal. Fail-closed (a miss is permanent and public once the repo is public); CLAUDE_DISABLE_CODENAME_GUARD=1 escape hatch for genuine false positives only.

items.title: Dispatch guard hook: agent briefs checked against the BOW before send
items.desc: claude-dispatch-guard.js (PreToolUse on the Agent tool): checks look-up-able facts in a dispatch brief before it is sent — cited BOW codes exist, a brief's stated module key agrees with that item's real BOW mkey, acceptance criteria the brief asks for don't already exist at docs/planning/acceptance/<mkey>.md, and declared file ownership doesn't overlap another live session's claim (via sync_file_claims) — with non-existent paths warned, not blocked. Fail-open (its own bug must not halt the team); CLAUDE_DISABLE_DISPATCH_GUARD=1 escape hatch. Born from an eight-error dispatch wave on 2026-08-10 where seven of eight errors were mechanically checkable facts asserted from memory.

items.title: Commit-identity guard hook: commits blocked when author/committer email isn't a sanctioned identity
items.desc: claude-author-guard.js (PreToolUse on git commit): derives a sanctioned email set at runtime — the configured `git config user.email` (unconditional), emails appearing >=3 times as author or committer in trunk history, and an operator-set CLAUDE_AUTHOR_GUARD_EXTRA_IDENTITIES extension list (GR#15: no hardcoded identities) — and denies a commit whose resolved author or committer email (explicit --author, GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env overrides, or config fallback) isn't in that set. Matches by email only, not name+email. Fail-closed; CLAUDE_DISABLE_AUTHOR_GUARD=1 escape hatch. Born from BUG-035 (a stray test-identity commit created locally on main the same day the repo went public and its history was rewritten to control identity).

items.title: AST-derived copy-guard CI gate: mechanically replaces the hand copyable-struct sweep
items.desc: internal/foundation/astgate/ (a real Go package, not a root Node hook — mirrors internal/foundation/errs/source_scan_test.go's AST-scan approach): walks cmd/ and internal/ source (excluding _test.go) to enumerate every candidate type (a struct mixing a sync.Mutex/RWMutex value field with an aliasable reference field) and every function that can receive one, by receiver METHOD OR by PACKAGE-LEVEL PARAMETER (the blind spot — errs.SetSink(l *Logger) — that let SEC-031 escape nine hand enumerations by four agents); flags any such function with no checkNotCopied-shaped identity guard as a hard CI violation, and separately flags (advisory-only) a guarded rejection path that writes into a shared bounded resource. No hardcoded type list or count (GR#15). Wired into the existing build-test-vet CI job per Bill's 2026-08-10 ruling (ASM-111). Filed under tool.* rather than foundation.errors deliberately (Bill's ruling on ASM-112): it is a cross-cutting repo-wide gate, not a package the code it audits belongs to.
